items.title: S&P 500 is expected to reach fresh highs this year — but Barclays warns of risks
items.content: Strategists at the bank warn of rising macroeconomic volatility, capital-supply concerns related to artificial intelligence and uncertainty over the U.S. midterm elections.

items.title: Does a 2% beneficiary inherit 100% if the 98% beneficiary dies in a car accident? Asking for a friend.
items.content: “I’m curious what would happen if the account owner were to die suddenly at the same time as the 98% beneficiary.”

items.title: Consumer spending posts smallest increase in seven months. Economy getting weaker?
items.content: Consumer spending rose in July at the slowest pace in seven months, suggesting the U.S. economy lost a little steam after the end of the 2026 Word Cup and start of the third quarter.

items.title: There’s so much betting against long-term bonds that a turnaround could catch investors off guard, says Citadel Securities
items.content: Citadel Securities’ strategist Frank Flight says a bet that appears to be one-sided against long-term bonds could be setting up for a painful unwind.

items.title: U.S. inflation rises again and stays well above Fed’s target. Rate hike might be in play.
items.content: The main inflation gauge used by the Federal Reserve to set U.S. interest rates rose at an elevated rate in July, potentially pushing the Federal Reserve closer to a vote to raise interest rates next month.

items.title: The renter generation: Young Americans, shut out of homeownership, brace to rent forever
items.content: People once believed if they worked hard, they could become homeowners, but ‘we’re coming to terms with the fact that perhaps most won’t. And that’s the new normal.’

items.title: Wall Street’s biggest optimist says he ‘wouldn’t jump into the AI trade right now’
items.content: Ed Yardeni, who has been called the most bullish person on Wall Street, says he hasn’t been bullish enough on the stock market.

items.title: Callaway Golf’s apology for ad showing woman being shoved to the ground exposes a major industry blind spot
items.content: The viral ad shows a male golfer pushing a female golfer to the ground. Since 2019, women and girls made up nearly 60% of net golfer growth.

items.title: I’m 56 with $1.4 million and want to retire in 5 years. Do I move to California, New York or overseas?
items.content: “How do I prepare for market drops or crashes just before or after retirement?”

items.title: ‘It’s the ultimate regifting’: My mom gave me a house. Should I transfer it back to her to reduce capital gains?
items.content: “The property is very old and requires significant ongoing maintenance.”
